audits.title: eP73 “Why Radiology Requests are not Being Accepted”, a quality improvement audit in a surgical department
audits.standard: Royal College of Radiologists guidance that requests include comprehensive relevant information
audits.setting: Surgical department, NHS Lanarkshire

cycle1.result: 73% (52/71) of radiology requests accepted; rejections due to inappropriate imaging (4/19), duplicate requests (4/19) and insufficient clinical details (4/19), each 21%.

audits.intervention: Structured request format developed and staff educated on its use.
audits.other_findings: not reported
audits.citation: Sajol M, El Salahi M, Ali K. eP73 “Why Radiology Requests are not Being Accepted”, a quality improvement audit in a surgical department. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_13). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf166.417.

audits.title: Prevalence of inadequate completion of computed tomography request forms submitted to public and private medical imaging centres in Ashanti Region of Ghana: a retrospective audit
audits.standard: Complete documentation of demographic, clinical, referrer and procedure information on CT request forms
audits.setting: One public and one private medical imaging centre, Kumasi

cycle1.result: Overall prevalence of inadequate completion 0.752 (95% CI 0.719-0.787); reason for referral documented on 391 (81.5%), highest in the private centre (96.7%).

audits.other_findings: Authors call for organisational system strengthening to improve form completion.

audits.title: Adequate Completion of Radiology Request Forms: A clinical Audit at Managil Teaching Hospital, Sudan
audits.standard: Royal College of Radiologists standard structured request form
audits.setting: Managil Teaching Hospital and three adjacent private radiology clinics

cycle1.result: Many request forms incomplete; patient's age written in 13% of forms.

audits.intervention: A ready (pre-designed) request form was introduced.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in most areas; patient's age written in 92% of forms.

audits.other_findings: not reported

audits.title: Inter-observer agreement in audit of quality of radiology requests and reports.
audits.standard: Standardised scoring system for request and report quality items
audits.setting: Department of Radiology, Akershus University Hospital

cycle1.result: Acceptable item scores above 70% for all items except requester bleep/extension, legibility of physician's name and previous investigation details.

audits.other_findings: Kappa values low despite high agreement (only 14 of 90 ratings > 0.60); 150 reports also reviewed.

audits.standard: Proforma based on national guidelines for temporal bone CT requests
audits.setting: Queen's Medical Centre, Nottingham (otolaryngology and neuroradiology)

cycle1.result: 52% of reports were clinically relevant.

audits.title: Improving the availability of clinical history accompanying radiographic examinations in a large pediatric radiology department.
audits.standard: 95% of clinical histories to contain what-when-where elements
audits.setting: Large paediatric radiology department, outpatient and emergency radiography, Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center

cycle1.result: 38% (76/200) had a complete clinical history.

audits.intervention: Technologists supplemented referrers' history; automated weekly audits with group then individual performance reports; quarterly results built into technologists' performance goals.
audits.other_findings: 92% (928/1006) complete by the end of the 15-week improvement phase.
audits.citation: Hawkins CM, Anton CG, Bankes WM, Leach AD, Zeno MJ, Pryor RM, et al.. Improving the availability of clinical history accompanying radiographic examinations in a large pediatric radiology department. AJR Am J Roentgenol. 2014;202(4):790-796. doi:10.2214/ajr.13.11273. PMID: 24660708.

audits.title: Quality use of diagnostic imaging in trauma, and the impact on emergency medical practice-a retrospective clinical audit.
audits.standard: American College of Radiology/European Society of Radiology imaging guidelines
audits.setting: Level 1 adult trauma centre emergency department, Westmead Hospital; retrospective audit

cycle1.result: 642 imaging decisions for 370 trauma cases; non-compliance was low. Non-compliant orders leading to change in management: JMOs 11 (65%), SRMOs 25 (53%), EMRs 12 (63%), consultants 11 (52%).

audits.other_findings: JMOs and SRMOs ordered more non-compliant imaging for conservatively managed than surgically managed patients.
audits.citation: Klein RP, Velan G, Young N, Shetty A, Moscova M. Quality use of diagnostic imaging in trauma, and the impact on emergency medical practice-a retrospective clinical audit. Emerg Radiol. 2021;28(4):761-770. doi:10.1007/s10140-021-01921-6. PMID: 33638062.

audits.standard: Royal College of Radiologists (RCR) standards for radiology request forms
audits.setting: Radiology Department, Atbara Police Hospital, Khartoum

cycle1.result: Mean documentation score 25.33%; patient address, phone number and location recorded in 0 (0%); age in 15 (30%).

audits.intervention: Blank paper request format replaced by a structured RCR-based form, distributed hospital-wide, with presentations and briefings for doctors.

cycle2.result: Mean documentation score 97.77%; address, phone number and location 50 (100%); age 50 (100%).

audits.other_findings: Some deficiencies persisted, prompting a call for orientation and follow-up training for physicians.

audits.title: Improving Clinical Information on Whole-Body CT Requests for Major Trauma: A Quality Improvement Study.
audits.standard: Royal College of Radiologists 2024 major trauma guidance: six minimum data elements for WBCT requests and RCR WBCT criteria
audits.setting: District general hospital (Kettering General Hospital NHS Foundation Trust), radiology and emergency departments

cycle1.result: Mechanism of injury 74%, primary survey 94%, haemodynamic status 7%, preceding investigations 5%, past medical history 13%, trauma team leader contact 0%; 57% of requests met RCR WBCT criteria

audits.intervention: Educational feedback to radiology and emergency medicine staff, RCR-derived electronic request proforma embedded in CareFlow EPR, and real-time radiologist feedback

cycle2.result: Mechanism of injury 100%; past medical history 18% (p = 0.329); preceding investigations 4% (p = 1.000); requests meeting RCR WBCT criteria 96%

audits.other_findings: Preceding investigations and past medical history documentation remained low after intervention.
audits.citation: Sansi RR, Naidu L, Ile IM, Naidu J. Improving Clinical Information on Whole-Body CT Requests for Major Trauma: A Quality Improvement Study. Br J Hosp Med (Lond). 2026;87(8):53482. doi:10.31083/bjhm53482. PMID: 42689904.

audits.title: Outpatient radiology imaging request quality using the reason for exam imaging reporting and data system (RI-RADS): A multicentre quality audit.
audits.standard: Reason for Exam Imaging Reporting and Data System (RI-RADS)
audits.setting: Outpatient radiology at multiple hospitals

cycle1.result: Only 18 requests (1.6%) achieved RI-RADS grade A (98.4% inadequate); grade D most frequent (51.9%); complete clinical information in only 2.2%.

audits.other_findings: Hospital was the strongest independent predictor of poor quality; orthopaedics had poorer request quality (OR = 3.59).
audits.citation: Abeshan SM, Alghamdi SB, Alshamrani S, Al Nawwar AM, Hejji NH, Alsulaiman YA, et al.. Outpatient radiology imaging request quality using the reason for exam imaging reporting and data system (RI-RADS): A multicentre quality audit.
